exercises.title: Asset directory
exercises.prompt: List the code and description of every equipment record.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code,
       description
FROM equipment
exercises.reason: Name only the columns a reader needs; each equipment row describes one asset.

exercises.title: Where work happens
exercises.prompt: List the distinct location names in equipment.
exercises.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT LOCATION
FROM equipment
exercises.reason: DISTINCT collapses repeated output values after selecting the location.

exercises.title: Open work
exercises.prompt: Return id and equipment_code for open work orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       equipment_code
FROM work_orders
WHERE status='Open'
exercises.reason: WHERE tests each order before it appears in the result.

exercises.title: High priority in Utilities
exercises.prompt: Return asset codes that are both High criticality and in Utilities.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code
FROM equipment
WHERE criticality='High'
  AND LOCATION='Utilities'
exercises.reason: Combine both tests with AND so an asset must satisfy each condition.

exercises.title: Two status bands
exercises.prompt: List codes for assets whose criticality is either High or Medium.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code
FROM equipment
WHERE criticality IN ('High',
                      'Medium')
exercises.reason: IN expresses a choice between a small set of allowed values.

exercises.title: Midrange costs
exercises.prompt: Return order ID and cost for orders costing 300 through 600 inclusive.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       cost
FROM work_orders
WHERE cost BETWEEN 300 AND 600
exercises.reason: BETWEEN includes both boundary amounts.

exercises.title: Pump codes
exercises.prompt: List equipment codes beginning with PUMP. Match the prefix regardless of suffix.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code
FROM equipment
WHERE code LIKE 'PUMP%'
exercises.reason: The trailing wildcard permits any remaining characters after the prefix.

exercises.title: Outside Production
exercises.prompt: Return code and location for assets outside Production.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code,
       LOCATION
FROM equipment
WHERE LOCATION <> 'Production'
exercises.reason: Use an inequality comparison on location.

exercises.title: Two costliest orders
exercises.prompt: List the two highest-cost orders as id and cost. Break ties with smaller IDs first. Preserve this order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       cost
FROM work_orders
ORDER BY cost DESC,
         id
LIMIT 2
exercises.reason: Sort before limiting. The ID tie-breaker makes the selection repeatable.

exercises.title: Count the backlog
exercises.prompt: Return a single count of open work orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM work_orders
WHERE status='Open'
exercises.reason: Filter to the backlog before counting the remaining rows.

exercises.title: Total booked hours
exercises.prompt: Return total hours from all labor_entries.
exercises.sql:
SELECT SUM(hours)
FROM labor_entries
exercises.reason: SUM adds the values across all bookings.

exercises.title: Typical order cost
exercises.prompt: Return average work-order cost rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(cost), 2)
FROM work_orders
exercises.reason: Round the aggregate once to avoid intermediate rounding errors.

exercises.title: Cost extremes
exercises.prompt: Return one row with the minimum and maximum work-order cost, in that order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT MIN(cost),
       MAX(cost)
FROM work_orders
exercises.reason: Two aggregates without grouping describe the same whole set.

exercises.title: Issue line value
exercises.prompt: For every material issue return ID and extended value: quantity times unit_cost.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       quantity*unit_cost
FROM material_issues
exercises.reason: Multiplication is evaluated separately on each issue line.

exercises.title: Reorder gap
exercises.prompt: For stock below its reorder level, return part, store and units short.
exercises.sql:
SELECT part,
       store,
       reorder_level-quantity
FROM stock
WHERE quantity<reorder_level
exercises.reason: Apply the threshold at part-store level before calculating the positive gap.

exercises.title: Case-normalized identifiers
exercises.prompt: Return each supplier code and its lowercase form.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code,
       LOWER(code)
FROM suppliers
exercises.reason: LOWER transforms the output while retaining the original identifier for comparison.

exercises.title: Description length
exercises.prompt: Return each asset code and the number of characters in its description.
exercises.sql:
SELECT code,
       LENGTH(description)
FROM equipment
exercises.reason: LENGTH counts text characters in SQLite.

exercises.title: Month label
exercises.prompt: For every meter reading, return id and its YYYY-MM month.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       SUBSTR(reading_date, 1, 7)
FROM meter_readings
exercises.reason: The ISO date starts with a four-digit year, a hyphen and a two-digit month.

exercises.title: Missing reviewer
exercises.prompt: List event IDs in order_events whose reviewer is NULL.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id
FROM order_events
WHERE reviewer IS NULL
exercises.reason: Test absence with IS NULL. Equality to NULL does not produce a true condition.

exercises.title: Reviewer fallback
exercises.prompt: For every order event return id and reviewer, displaying Unassigned when reviewer is NULL.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       COALESCE(reviewer, 'Unassigned')
FROM order_events
exercises.reason: COALESCE selects its first non-null argument.

exercises.title: Cost bands
exercises.prompt: Return id and the label Large for orders costing at least 500, otherwise Standard.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       CASE
           WHEN cost>=500 THEN 'Large'
           ELSE 'Standard'
       END
FROM work_orders
exercises.reason: CASE maps a numeric rule to a readable category.

exercises.title: Receipt chronology
exercises.prompt: Return receipt id, po and quantity with the newest ID first. Preserve this order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       po,
       quantity
FROM receipts
ORDER BY id DESC
exercises.reason: A descending key traverses the imported receipt IDs from largest to smallest.

exercises.title: Distinct assets with work
exercises.prompt: Return the number of different equipment codes appearing in work orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT equipment_code)
FROM work_orders
exercises.reason: Counting distinct equipment answers a different question from counting orders.

exercises.title: Inspection outcomes
exercises.prompt: Return result and number of inspections for each result value.
exercises.sql:
SELECT RESULT,
       COUNT(*)
FROM inspections
GROUP BY RESULT
exercises.reason: Grouping changes the output from one row per inspection to one per outcome.

exercises.title: Parts used twice
exercises.prompt: List part and total issued quantity for parts whose combined issued quantity is at least two.
exercises.sql:
SELECT part,
       SUM(quantity)
FROM material_issues
GROUP BY part
HAVING SUM(quantity)>=2
exercises.reason: HAVING filters totals after each part group is formed.

exercises.title: Name the equipment
exercises.prompt: For each work order return order id, equipment description and status.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.id,
       e.description,
       w.status
FROM work_orders w
JOIN equipment e ON e.code=w.equipment_code
exercises.reason: Attach the equipment description using the asset primary key.

exercises.title: Find the employer organization
exercises.prompt: For each department return department code and owning organization name.
exercises.sql:
SELECT d.code,
       o.name
FROM departments d
JOIN organizations o ON o.code=d.org
exercises.reason: The organization code is the link from a department to its single owner.

exercises.title: Bookings by trade
exercises.prompt: Return trade and total booked hours grouped by the employee’s assigned trade.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.trade,
       SUM(l.hours)
FROM labor_entries l
JOIN employees e ON e.code=l.employee
GROUP BY e.trade
exercises.reason: Join the employee for classification, then aggregate the booking rows.

exercises.title: Supplier spend
exercises.prompt: For suppliers with purchase lines, return supplier code and total ordered value.
exercises.sql:
SELECT p.supplier,
       SUM(l.quantity*l.unit_price)
FROM purchase_orders p
JOIN purchase_lines l ON l.po=p.id
GROUP BY p.supplier
exercises.reason: Calculate value at line level before rolling it up to supplier.

exercises.title: Include idle assets
exercises.prompt: Return every asset code and its count of work orders, including zero.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.code,
       COUNT(w.id)
FROM equipment e
LEFT JOIN work_orders w ON w.equipment_code=e.code
GROUP BY e.code
exercises.reason: Count a matched order ID so the preserved empty asset contributes zero.

exercises.title: Uninspected equipment
exercises.prompt: Return codes of assets with no inspection record.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.code
FROM equipment e
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM inspections i
     WHERE i.equipment=e.code)
exercises.reason: An anti-join keeps an asset when the correlated lookup finds no inspection.

exercises.title: Orders with materials
exercises.prompt: Return IDs of work orders with at least one material issue, once per order.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.id
FROM work_orders w
WHERE EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM material_issues m
     WHERE m.wo=w.id)
exercises.reason: EXISTS tests membership without multiplying an order by its issue count.

exercises.title: Above the mean
exercises.prompt: Return id and cost for orders costing strictly more than the overall order average.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       cost
FROM work_orders
WHERE cost>
    (SELECT AVG(cost)
     FROM work_orders)
exercises.reason: A scalar subquery supplies one threshold to every outer row.

exercises.title: Store totals
exercises.prompt: Return store, total on-hand units and distinct stocked part count per store.
exercises.sql:
SELECT store,
       SUM(quantity),
       COUNT(DISTINCT part)
FROM stock
GROUP BY store
exercises.reason: The two aggregates measure volume and assortment separately.

exercises.title: Open and closed counts
exercises.prompt: For every equipment code present in work_orders return code, open count and closed count.
exercises.sql:
SELECT equipment_code,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN status='Open' THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END),
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN status='Closed' THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END)
FROM work_orders
GROUP BY equipment_code
exercises.reason: Conditional sums create status columns without filtering away other rows.

exercises.title: Line receipt balance
exercises.prompt: For every purchase line return po, line and ordered quantity less cumulative receipts. Include unreceived lines.
exercises.sql:
SELECT l.po,
       l.line,
       l.quantity-COALESCE(SUM(r.quantity), 0)
FROM purchase_lines l
LEFT JOIN receipts r ON r.po=l.po
AND r.line=l.line
GROUP BY l.po,
         l.line,
         l.quantity
exercises.reason: Use the two-part line identity; an absent receipt contributes zero.

exercises.title: Monthly reading count
exercises.prompt: Return meter, YYYY-MM and count of readings for each observed meter-month.
exercises.sql:
SELECT meter,
       strftime('%Y-%m', reading_date),
       COUNT(*)
FROM meter_readings
GROUP BY meter,
         strftime('%Y-%m', reading_date)
exercises.reason: Extract the month before grouping and retain the meter identifier.

exercises.title: Unreserved stock lines
exercises.prompt: List part and store combinations in stock with no matching reservation.
exercises.sql:
SELECT part,
       store
FROM stock
EXCEPT
SELECT part,
       store
FROM reservations
exercises.reason: EXCEPT compares complete two-column keys.

exercises.title: Parts in both flows
exercises.prompt: Return distinct part codes appearing in both purchase_lines and material_issues.
exercises.sql:
SELECT part
FROM purchase_lines INTERSECT
SELECT part
FROM material_issues
exercises.reason: INTERSECT returns the keys common to the two sets.

exercises.title: All part demand
exercises.prompt: List distinct part codes found in requisition_lines or reservations.
exercises.sql:
SELECT part
FROM requisition_lines
UNION
SELECT part
FROM reservations
exercises.reason: UNION removes duplicates both within and between inputs.

exercises.title: Signed movement ledger
exercises.prompt: Return part and total signed units using receipts as positive and issues as negative. Recover receipt part from the purchase line.
exercises.sql:
SELECT part,
       SUM(delta)
FROM
  (SELECT l.part,
          r.quantity AS delta
   FROM receipts r
   JOIN purchase_lines l ON l.po=r.po
   AND l.line=r.line
   UNION ALL SELECT part,-quantity
   FROM material_issues)
GROUP BY part
exercises.reason: UNION ALL preserves distinct transactions that happen to carry equal quantities.

exercises.title: Labor value
exercises.prompt: Return work order number and total actual labor value for orders with bookings.
exercises.sql:
SELECT wo,
       SUM(hours*rate)
FROM labor_entries
GROUP BY wo
exercises.reason: Use the rate recorded on each booking before aggregating.

exercises.title: Nominal versus booked rate
exercises.prompt: For each booking return id, recorded rate and nominal trade rate of the employee.
exercises.sql:
SELECT l.id,
       l.rate,
       t.hourly_rate
FROM labor_entries l
JOIN employees e ON e.code=l.employee
JOIN trades t ON t.code=e.trade
exercises.reason: Two joins connect the booking to its assigned trade without rewriting the historical rate.

exercises.title: Material share of cost
exercises.prompt: For orders with issues return order ID and issued value as a percentage of order cost rounded to one decimal. Use NULL for zero cost.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.id,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(m.quantity*m.unit_cost)/NULLIF(w.cost, 0), 1)
FROM work_orders w
JOIN material_issues m ON m.wo=w.id
GROUP BY w.id,
         w.cost
exercises.reason: A decimal numerator avoids integer division and NULLIF protects a zero denominator.

exercises.title: Equipment status summary
exercises.prompt: Return each location and the number of distinct assets there with at least one open order. Include locations represented in equipment with zero open orders.
exercises.sql:
SELECT e.location,
       COUNT(DISTINCT w.equipment_code)
FROM equipment e
LEFT JOIN work_orders w ON w.equipment_code=e.code
AND w.status='Open'
GROUP BY e.location
exercises.reason: Put the status test in the join so locations without open orders survive.

exercises.title: Latest inspection ID
exercises.prompt: For every inspected asset return equipment code and the result associated with its highest inspection ID.
exercises.sql:
SELECT i.equipment,
       i.result
FROM inspections i
WHERE i.id=
    (SELECT MAX(j.id)
     FROM inspections j
     WHERE j.equipment=i.equipment)
exercises.reason: Find the highest ID for the same asset before retrieving the corresponding result.

exercises.title: Active suppliers without orders
exercises.prompt: List all supplier codes with no purchase order in the dataset.
exercises.sql:
SELECT s.code
FROM suppliers s
LEFT JOIN purchase_orders p ON p.supplier=s.code
WHERE p.id IS NULL
exercises.reason: A missing right-side primary key identifies the unmatched supplier.

exercises.title: Approval share
exercises.prompt: For each org appearing in requisitions return org and percentage of requisitions Approved, rounded to one decimal.
exercises.sql:
SELECT org,
       ROUND(100.0*AVG(CASE
                           WHEN status='Approved' THEN 1
                           ELSE 0
                       END), 1)
FROM requisitions
GROUP BY org
exercises.reason: The average of a zero-or-one indicator is the share of matching records.

exercises.title: Calendar delay
exercises.prompt: For every event dated after 2026-01-01 return id and integer days elapsed since that date.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       CAST(julianday(event_date)-julianday('2026-01-01') AS INTEGER)
FROM order_events
WHERE event_date>'2026-01-01'
exercises.reason: Subtract Julian-day values to measure the interval across month boundaries.

exercises.title: Asset comparison pairs
exercises.prompt: Return each pair of different assets sharing a location as smaller code, larger code. Include each pair once.
exercises.sql:
SELECT a.code,
       b.code
FROM equipment a
JOIN equipment b ON a.location=b.location
AND a.code<b.code
exercises.reason: The strict ordering excludes self-pairs and reversed duplicates in one condition.

exercises.title: Net available inventory
exercises.prompt: For every stock row return part, store and quantity less reserved units at that same part and store.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT part,
          store,
          SUM(quantity) n
   FROM reservations
   GROUP BY part,
            store)
SELECT s.part,
       s.store,
       s.quantity-COALESCE(r.n, 0)
FROM stock s
LEFT JOIN r ON r.part=s.part
AND r.store=s.store
exercises.reason: Reduce reservations to the stock grain before attaching their total.

exercises.title: Two independent cost streams
exercises.prompt: For every order return id, booked labor value and issued material value. Supply zero for missing streams.
exercises.sql:
WITH l AS
  (SELECT wo,
          SUM(hours*rate) n
   FROM labor_entries
   GROUP BY wo),
     m AS
  (SELECT wo,
          SUM(quantity*unit_cost) n
   FROM material_issues
   GROUP BY wo)
SELECT w.id,
       COALESCE(l.n, 0),
       COALESCE(m.n, 0)
FROM work_orders w
LEFT JOIN l ON l.wo=w.id
LEFT JOIN m ON m.wo=w.id
exercises.reason: Aggregate each detail stream first. Joining raw bookings to raw issues creates a cross product.

exercises.title: Activity variance
exercises.prompt: Return wo, activity and actual minus planned hours for every planned activity, including work with zero booked time.
exercises.sql:
SELECT a.wo,
       a.activity,
       COALESCE(SUM(l.hours), 0)-a.planned_hours
FROM activities a
LEFT JOIN labor_entries l ON l.wo=a.wo
AND l.activity=a.activity
GROUP BY a.wo,
         a.activity,
         a.planned_hours
exercises.reason: Both parts of the activity key are required. An unbooked activity has negative variance.

exercises.title: Cost rank within status
exercises.prompt: Return id, status and dense cost rank within status, highest cost first. Ties share a rank.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       status,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY status
                         ORDER BY cost DESC)
FROM work_orders
exercises.reason: Partitioning restarts the ranking and dense ranks advance without gaps.

exercises.title: Top two per location
exercises.prompt: Return location, order ID and cost for at most two highest-cost orders per location. Break ties by lower ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT e.location,
          w.id,
          w.cost,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY e.location
                            ORDER BY w.cost DESC, w.id) n
   FROM work_orders w
   JOIN equipment e ON e.code=w.equipment_code)
SELECT LOCATION,
       id,
       cost
FROM x
WHERE n<=2
exercises.reason: Assign deterministic positions within each location, then filter in an outer query.

exercises.title: Meter increments
exercises.prompt: Return meter, reading ID and change from its previous reading in date and ID sequence. Keep NULL for the first.
exercises.sql:
SELECT meter,
       id,
       reading-LAG(reading) OVER(PARTITION BY meter
                                 ORDER BY reading_date, id)
FROM meter_readings
exercises.reason: LAG looks at the prior row within the same meter’s sequence.

exercises.title: Running issued value
exercises.prompt: Return issue ID, work order and cumulative issued value within that order in ascending issue ID sequence.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       wo,
       SUM(quantity*unit_cost) OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                                    ORDER BY id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
FROM material_issues
exercises.reason: An explicit row frame includes all earlier issue rows and the current one.

exercises.title: Last three readings
exercises.prompt: Return reading ID and trailing average of up to three readings for the same meter, rounded to two decimals. Order the window by date then ID.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       ROUND(AVG(reading) OVER(PARTITION BY meter
                               ORDER BY reading_date, id ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW), 2)
FROM meter_readings
exercises.reason: ROWS counts observations, so sparse dates still contribute the last three recorded values.

exercises.title: Latest status per order
exercises.prompt: For every order with events return wo, latest event_date and status. Break same-date ties by highest event ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                            ORDER BY event_date DESC, id DESC) n
   FROM order_events)
SELECT wo,
       event_date,
       status
FROM x
WHERE n=1
exercises.reason: A deterministic row number retrieves the whole latest event.

exercises.title: Time to next event
exercises.prompt: Return event ID and the whole days until the next event for the same order, in date and ID sequence. Keep NULL at the end.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       CAST(julianday(LEAD(event_date) OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                                            ORDER BY event_date, id))-julianday(event_date) AS INTEGER)
FROM order_events
exercises.reason: LEAD provides the next date; subtract the current date to measure elapsed days.

exercises.title: First versus current reading
exercises.prompt: Return each reading ID and difference from that meter’s very first reading by date and ID.
exercises.sql:
SELECT id,
       reading-FIRST_VALUE(reading) OVER(PARTITION BY meter
                                         ORDER BY reading_date, id)
FROM meter_readings
exercises.reason: FIRST_VALUE holds the baseline fixed while the current reading advances.

exercises.title: Category contribution
exercises.prompt: Return status and its percentage of total work-order cost rounded to two decimals. Return NULL when the total is zero.
exercises.sql:
SELECT status,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(cost)/NULLIF(SUM(SUM(cost)) OVER(), 0), 2)
FROM work_orders
GROUP BY status
exercises.reason: Group first; the window sum then acts on group totals.

exercises.title: Above location average
exercises.prompt: Return order id, location and cost for orders strictly above their own location’s average order cost.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT w.id,
          e.location,
          w.cost,
          AVG(w.cost) OVER(PARTITION BY e.location) avg_cost
   FROM work_orders w
   JOIN equipment e ON e.code=w.equipment_code)
SELECT id,
       LOCATION,
       cost
FROM x
WHERE cost>avg_cost
exercises.reason: A partition average annotates every order without collapsing it into a group.

exercises.title: Maximum-cost ties
exercises.prompt: Return equipment_code, id and cost for every order tied for highest cost on its own asset.
exercises.sql:
SELECT equipment_code,
       id,
       cost
FROM work_orders w
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM work_orders v
     WHERE v.equipment_code=w.equipment_code
       AND v.cost>w.cost)
exercises.reason: A maximum has no strictly larger peer, which retains every tie.

exercises.title: Stores stocking all parts
exercises.prompt: Return store codes stocking every part in the parts master, regardless of quantity.
exercises.sql:
SELECT s.code
FROM stores s
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM parts p
     WHERE NOT EXISTS
         (SELECT 1
          FROM stock x
          WHERE x.store=s.code
            AND x.part=p.code))
exercises.reason: Double NOT EXISTS expresses that no required part is missing.

exercises.title: Positive outstanding lines
exercises.prompt: For each supplier with purchase lines return supplier and number of lines with a positive unreceived balance, including zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT po,
          LINE,
          SUM(quantity) qty
   FROM receipts
   GROUP BY po,
            LINE)
SELECT p.supplier,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN l.quantity>COALESCE(r.qty, 0) THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END)
FROM purchase_orders p
JOIN purchase_lines l ON l.po=p.id
LEFT JOIN r ON r.po=l.po
AND r.line=l.line
GROUP BY p.supplier
exercises.reason: Compute the received amount once per line before counting exceptions.

exercises.title: Current stock coverage
exercises.prompt: For every part in stock return part and count of stores where on-hand less reservations meets or exceeds reorder level.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT part,
          store,
          SUM(quantity) q
   FROM reservations
   GROUP BY part,
            store)
SELECT s.part,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN s.quantity-COALESCE(r.q, 0)>=s.reorder_level THEN 1
               ELSE 0
           END)
FROM stock s
LEFT JOIN r ON r.part=s.part
AND r.store=s.store
GROUP BY s.part
exercises.reason: Evaluate coverage independently at each store before summing successes.

exercises.title: Receipt-weighted price
exercises.prompt: For each received part return part and average unit price weighted by received units, rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql:
SELECT l.part,
       ROUND(SUM(l.unit_price*r.quantity)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(r.quantity), 0), 2)
FROM receipts r
JOIN purchase_lines l ON l.po=r.po
AND l.line=r.line
GROUP BY l.part
exercises.reason: Weight the agreed line price by units actually received.

exercises.title: Repeated status events
exercises.prompt: List event ID and wo when the event status equals the immediately preceding status for that order in date and ID sequence.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(status) OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                           ORDER BY event_date, id) prev
   FROM order_events)
SELECT id,
       wo
FROM x
WHERE status=prev
exercises.reason: LAG compares neighboring observations instead of all events with the same status.

exercises.title: Earliest closure
exercises.prompt: For orders with a Closed event return wo, first event date and first Closed event date.
exercises.sql:
SELECT wo,
       MIN(event_date),
       MIN(CASE
               WHEN status='Closed' THEN event_date
           END)
FROM order_events
GROUP BY wo
HAVING COUNT(CASE
                 WHEN status='Closed' THEN 1
             END)>0
exercises.reason: Conditional MIN picks the earliest closure while unrestricted MIN retains the true start.

exercises.title: Status transitions
exercises.prompt: Return previous status, new status and number of actual changes across all orders. Ignore first events and unchanged statuses.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT status,
          LAG(status) OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                           ORDER BY event_date, id) prev
   FROM order_events)
SELECT prev,
       status,
       COUNT(*)
FROM x
WHERE prev<>status
GROUP BY prev,
         status
exercises.reason: First derive neighboring pairs within each order, then pool comparable transitions.

exercises.title: Locations with complete inspection coverage
exercises.prompt: Return locations where every asset has at least one inspection.
exercises.sql:
SELECT LOCATION
FROM equipment e
GROUP BY LOCATION
HAVING COUNT(*)=SUM(CASE
                        WHEN EXISTS
                               (SELECT 1
                                FROM inspections i
                                WHERE i.equipment=e.code) THEN 1
                        ELSE 0
                    END)
exercises.reason: Compare the asset count with the number of assets having evidence; multiple inspections still count once.

exercises.title: Monthly milestone
exercises.prompt: For each meter-month return meter, YYYY-MM and its last recorded reading by date then ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          strftime('%Y-%m', reading_date) m,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY meter, strftime('%Y-%m', reading_date)
                            ORDER BY reading_date DESC, id DESC) n
   FROM meter_readings)
SELECT meter,
       m,
       reading
FROM x
WHERE n=1
exercises.reason: Use the latest observation, even when a reset makes it smaller than an earlier reading.

exercises.title: Project utilization
exercises.prompt: For every project return code, budget and percent of budget represented by its linked work-order costs, rounded to two decimals. Use zero spend for projects without work and NULL for zero budgets.
exercises.sql:
SELECT p.code,
       p.budget,
       ROUND(100.0*COALESCE(SUM(w.cost), 0)/NULLIF(p.budget, 0), 2)
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN work_projects x ON x.project=p.code
LEFT JOIN work_orders w ON w.id=x.wo
GROUP BY p.code,
         p.budget
exercises.reason: Start from projects so an empty project survives both joins.

exercises.title: Days without events
exercises.prompt: Return every date from 2026-01-01 to 2026-01-10 inclusive on which no order event occurred.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE days(d) AS
  (SELECT '2026-01-01'
   UNION ALL SELECT date(d, '+1 day')
   FROM days
   WHERE d<'2026-01-10')
SELECT d
FROM days
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM order_events e
     WHERE e.event_date=d)
exercises.reason: Generate the complete calendar, then subtract dates with observations.

exercises.title: Compress the event history
exercises.prompt: Return wo, status, first date, last date and event count for each consecutive run of the same status. Sequence each order by event date then ID.
exercises.sql:
WITH a AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(status) OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                           ORDER BY event_date, id) prev
   FROM order_events),
     b AS
  (SELECT *,
          SUM(CASE
                  WHEN status=prev THEN 0
                  ELSE 1
              END) OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                        ORDER BY event_date, id) grp
   FROM a)
SELECT wo,
       status,
       MIN(event_date),
       MAX(event_date),
       COUNT(*)
FROM b
GROUP BY wo,
         grp,
         status
exercises.reason: Mark the first row of each run, cumulatively number the marks and aggregate within each run.

exercises.title: Longest daily streak
exercises.prompt: For each order with events return wo and the length of its longest streak of consecutive distinct event dates.
exercises.sql:
WITH d AS
  (SELECT DISTINCT wo,
                   event_date
   FROM order_events),
     g AS
  (SELECT *,
          julianday(event_date)-ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                                                  ORDER BY event_date) k
   FROM d),
     n AS
  (SELECT wo,
          k,
          COUNT(*) LEN
   FROM g
   GROUP BY wo,
            k)
SELECT wo,
       MAX(LEN)
FROM n
GROUP BY wo
exercises.reason: Deduplicate dates before subtracting row number from day number. Consecutive days share an island key.

exercises.title: Reopening after closure
exercises.prompt: For each change from Closed to Open return wo, reopening ID and integer days since the immediately preceding Closed event. Use date then ID sequence.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(status) OVER w prev,
          LAG(event_date) OVER w prev_date
   FROM order_events WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY wo
                                  ORDER BY event_date,
                                           id))
SELECT wo,
       id,
       CAST(julianday(event_date)-julianday(prev_date) AS INTEGER)
FROM x
WHERE status='Open'
  AND prev='Closed'
exercises.reason: Calculate both previous values before filtering so the closure remains in the window.

exercises.title: As-of snapshot
exercises.prompt: Return each work order’s ID and last event status on or before 2026-01-05. Use NULL if unknown, and highest ID to break same-day ties.
exercises.sql:
SELECT w.id,
  (SELECT e.status
   FROM order_events e
   WHERE e.wo=w.id
     AND e.event_date<='2026-01-05'
   ORDER BY e.event_date DESC,
            e.id DESC
   LIMIT 1)
FROM work_orders w
exercises.reason: Restrict history to the cutoff before selecting its latest event. Drive the result from all orders.

exercises.title: Daily open backlog
exercises.prompt: For each date from 2026-01-01 through 2026-01-10 return date and count of work orders whose latest known status by that day’s end was Open. Highest ID wins date ties. Exclude unknown states from the count.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(DAY) AS
  (SELECT '2026-01-01'
   UNION ALL SELECT date(DAY, '+1 day')
   FROM d
   WHERE DAY<'2026-01-10')
SELECT DAY,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM work_orders w
   WHERE
       (SELECT status
        FROM order_events e
        WHERE e.wo=w.id
          AND e.event_date<=d.day
        ORDER BY event_date DESC,
                 id DESC
        LIMIT 1)='Open')
FROM d
exercises.reason: Generate reporting days and carry forward the most recent state separately for each order.

exercises.title: Time spent open
exercises.prompt: Return wo and whole days in Open status across event intervals for every order with events. Close the final interval at 2026-02-01. Use date then ID sequence; same-day intervals contribute zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LEAD(event_date, 1, '2026-02-01') OVER(PARTITION BY wo
                                                 ORDER BY event_date, id) STOP
   FROM order_events)
SELECT wo,
       CAST(SUM(CASE
                    WHEN status='Open' THEN julianday(STOP)-julianday(event_date)
                    ELSE 0
                END) AS INTEGER)
FROM x
GROUP BY wo
exercises.reason: An event establishes status until the next event. Sum durations only for the intervals beginning open.

exercises.title: Median order cost
exercises.prompt: Return status and median order cost per status, averaging the two middle costs when the count is even.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY status
                            ORDER BY cost, id) n,
                       COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY status) cnt
   FROM work_orders)
SELECT status,
       AVG(cost)
FROM x
WHERE n IN ((cnt+1)/2,
            (cnt+2)/2)
GROUP BY status
exercises.reason: SQLite integer division yields the middle positions for odd and even groups.

exercises.title: Pareto cutoff
exercises.prompt: Return equipment code and total cost for the smallest prefix of assets with work that reaches at least 80 percent of total cost. Sort by descending asset total then code to resolve ties. Assume positive overall cost.
exercises.sql:
WITH a AS
  (SELECT equipment_code,
          SUM(cost) v
   FROM work_orders
   GROUP BY equipment_code),
     b AS
  (SELECT *,
          SUM(v) OVER(
                      ORDER BY v DESC, equipment_code) running,
                 SUM(v) OVER() total
   FROM a)
SELECT equipment_code,
       v
FROM b
WHERE running-v<0.8*total
exercises.reason: Test the total before adding the current asset. This includes the asset that crosses the threshold.

exercises.title: Exclude the current order
exercises.prompt: For orders having another order on the same asset, return ID and average cost of all other orders on that asset rounded to two decimals.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          SUM(cost) OVER(PARTITION BY equipment_code) total,
                    COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY equipment_code) n
   FROM work_orders)
SELECT id,
       ROUND((total-cost)*1.0/(n-1), 2)
FROM x
WHERE n>1
exercises.reason: Remove one value and one observation from the partition totals; singletons have no comparison.

exercises.title: Meter reset correction
exercises.prompt: For every meter return meter and accumulated usage across successive readings. A decrease indicates a reset to zero; count the new reading as the usage since reset. The first reading contributes zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(reading) OVER(PARTITION BY meter
                            ORDER BY reading_date, id) prev
   FROM meter_readings)
SELECT meter,
       SUM(CASE
               WHEN prev IS NULL THEN 0
               WHEN reading<prev THEN reading
               ELSE reading-prev
           END)
FROM x
GROUP BY meter
exercises.reason: Handle baseline, reset and normal increment separately before summing.

exercises.title: Peak daily consumption
exercises.prompt: For each meter return meter, ending reading ID and highest usage per elapsed day rounded to two decimals. Use successive observations ordered by date then ID. Ignore resets and zero-day intervals. Resolve equal rates by smaller ending ID; omit meters without eligible intervals.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT *,
          LAG(reading) OVER w pv,
          LAG(reading_date) OVER w pd
   FROM meter_readings WINDOW w AS(PARTITION BY meter
                                   ORDER BY reading_date,
                                            id)),
     y AS
  (SELECT *,
          (reading-pv)/(julianday(reading_date)-julianday(pd)) rate
   FROM x
   WHERE reading>=pv
     AND reading_date>pd),
     z AS
  (SELECT *,
          ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY meter
                            ORDER BY rate DESC, id) n
   FROM y)
SELECT meter,
       id,
       ROUND(rate, 2)
FROM z
WHERE n=1
exercises.reason: Rank unrounded rates after eliminating intervals with invalid duration or reset behavior.

exercises.title: Seven-day event volume
exercises.prompt: For each observed event date return date and number of events in the inclusive seven-calendar-day window ending that day.
exercises.sql:
WITH d AS
  (SELECT event_date,
          COUNT(*) n
   FROM order_events
   GROUP BY event_date)
SELECT event_date,
       SUM(n) OVER(
                   ORDER BY julianday(event_date) RANGE BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
FROM d
exercises.reason: RANGE operates on elapsed days; seven prior result rows could span far more than a week.

exercises.title: Cumulative unique orders
exercises.prompt: For each observed event date return date and number of distinct work orders observed up to and including that date.
exercises.sql:
WITH first_seen AS
  (SELECT wo,
          MIN(event_date) first_day
   FROM order_events
   GROUP BY wo),
     days AS
  (SELECT DISTINCT event_date
   FROM order_events)
SELECT event_date,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM first_seen
   WHERE first_day<=days.event_date)
FROM days
exercises.reason: Each order enters the cumulative population just once on its first date.

exercises.title: Depth of descendants
exercises.prompt: Starting at COOL-SYS, return every distinct reachable child and its minimum positive edge count. The training hierarchy is acyclic.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x(node, depth) AS
  (SELECT child,
          1
   FROM equipment_links
   WHERE parent='COOL-SYS'
   UNION ALL SELECT l.child,
                    x.depth+1
   FROM x
   JOIN equipment_links l ON l.parent=x.node)
SELECT node,
       MIN(depth)
FROM x
GROUP BY node
exercises.reason: Walk down child links and keep the shortest path when a node is reachable by several routes.

exercises.title: Roll costs up the hierarchy
exercises.prompt: Return one total cost across work orders on all descendants of COOL-SYS. Count each descendant’s orders once, even if two paths reach it. Exclude the root.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x(node) AS
  (SELECT child
   FROM equipment_links
   WHERE parent='COOL-SYS'
   UNION SELECT l.child
   FROM equipment_links l
   JOIN x ON l.parent=x.node)
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost), 0)
FROM work_orders
WHERE equipment_code IN
    (SELECT node
     FROM x)
exercises.reason: UNION collapses duplicate node identities before the financial aggregation.

exercises.title: Find terminal descendants
exercises.prompt: Return distinct descendants reachable from COOL-SYS that have no children of their own.
exercises.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE x(node) AS
  (SELECT child
   FROM equipment_links
   WHERE parent='COOL-SYS'
   UNION SELECT l.child
   FROM equipment_links l
   JOIN x ON l.parent=x.node)
SELECT node
FROM x
WHERE NOT EXISTS
    (SELECT 1
     FROM equipment_links l
     WHERE l.parent=x.node)
exercises.reason: Traverse first; a reachable node is a leaf when no edge starts there.

exercises.title: Fulfillment classification
exercises.prompt: For every purchase order with lines return ID and class: Over if any line is over-received, Complete if every line exactly matches, None if total receipts are zero, otherwise Partial. Apply rules in this order.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT po,
          LINE,
          SUM(quantity) q
   FROM receipts
   GROUP BY po,
            LINE),
     a AS
  (SELECT l.po,
          l.quantity,
          COALESCE(r.q, 0) q
   FROM purchase_lines l
   LEFT JOIN r ON r.po=l.po
   AND r.line=l.line)
SELECT po,
       CASE
           WHEN MAX(q>quantity)=1 THEN 'Over'
           WHEN MIN(q=quantity)=1 THEN 'Complete'
           WHEN SUM(q)=0 THEN 'None'
           ELSE 'Partial'
       END
FROM a
GROUP BY po
exercises.reason: Compare at line level before classifying an order. Over-delivery on one line cannot cancel a shortage on another.

exercises.title: FIFO reservation allocation
exercises.prompt: For each reservation return ID and units that can be filled from its part-store on-hand stock. Allocate to smaller reservation IDs first. Missing stock means zero and partial allocation is allowed.
exercises.sql:
WITH x AS
  (SELECT r.*,
          SUM(r.quantity) OVER(PARTITION BY r.part, r.store
                               ORDER BY r.id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)-r.quantity
   PRIOR
   FROM reservations r)
SELECT x.id,
       MAX(0, MIN(x.quantity, COALESCE(s.quantity, 0)-x.prior))
FROM x
LEFT JOIN stock s ON s.part=x.part
AND s.store=x.store
exercises.reason: Subtract earlier demand from starting stock, then clamp the available amount between zero and this request.

exercises.title: Move stock between stores
exercises.prompt: For every ordered pair of different stores stocking the same part, return part, donor, recipient and transferable units only when positive. Keep the donor at its reorder level and cap the transfer at the recipient’s shortage. Evaluate pairs independently.
exercises.sql:
SELECT d.part,
       d.store,
       r.store,
       MIN(d.quantity-d.reorder_level, r.reorder_level-r.quantity)
FROM stock d
JOIN stock r ON d.part=r.part
AND d.store<>r.store
WHERE d.quantity>d.reorder_level
  AND r.quantity<r.reorder_level
exercises.reason: A valid pair needs both a surplus and a shortage. The smaller quantity limits its independent transfer.

exercises.title: Allocate shared project cost
exercises.prompt: Split each linked work order’s cost equally across its linked projects. Return every project code and allocated cost rounded to two decimals, including zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH a AS
  (SELECT x.project,
          w.cost*1.0/COUNT(*) OVER(PARTITION BY x.wo) SHARE
   FROM work_projects x
   JOIN work_orders w ON w.id=x.wo)
SELECT p.code,
       ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(a.share), 0), 2)
FROM projects p
LEFT JOIN a ON a.project=p.code
GROUP BY p.code
exercises.reason: Divide at work-order grain before summing shares by project to conserve total cost.

exercises.title: Largest cost component
exercises.prompt: For each work order return id and largest of Labor, Material and Other. Other equals order cost less booked labor and issued material. Break ties in the listed order. Missing detail totals are zero.
exercises.sql:
WITH l AS
  (SELECT wo,
          SUM(hours*rate) v
   FROM labor_entries
   GROUP BY wo),
     m AS
  (SELECT wo,
          SUM(quantity*unit_cost) v
   FROM material_issues
   GROUP BY wo),
     a AS
  (SELECT w.id,
          w.cost,
          COALESCE(l.v, 0) labor,
          COALESCE(m.v, 0) mat
   FROM work_orders w
   LEFT JOIN l ON l.wo=w.id
   LEFT JOIN m ON m.wo=w.id)
SELECT id,
       CASE
           WHEN labor>=mat
                AND labor>=cost-labor-mat THEN 'Labor'
           WHEN mat>=cost-labor-mat THEN 'Material'
           ELSE 'Other'
       END
FROM a
exercises.reason: Reconcile independent detail totals first. The order of CASE conditions implements the tie rule.

exercises.title: First crossing of budget
exercises.prompt: For projects with a crossing, return project code and first work-order ID where cumulative linked order costs in ID order strictly exceed budget. Use full cost per linked order.
exercises.sql:
WITH a AS
  (SELECT p.code,
          p.budget,
          x.wo,
          SUM(w.cost) OVER(PARTITION BY p.code
                           ORDER BY x.wo) total
   FROM projects p
   JOIN work_projects x ON x.project=p.code
   JOIN work_orders w ON w.id=x.wo)
SELECT code,
       MIN(wo)
FROM a
WHERE total>budget
GROUP BY code
exercises.reason: Window the ordered costs per project before locating the first qualifying order.

exercises.title: Matched parts never fully supplied
exercises.prompt: Return distinct part codes that have purchase lines and for which every purchase line has received strictly fewer units than ordered.
exercises.sql:
WITH r AS
  (SELECT po,
          LINE,
          SUM(quantity) q
   FROM receipts
   GROUP BY po,
            LINE),
     a AS
  (SELECT l.part,
          l.quantity,
          COALESCE(r.q, 0) received
   FROM purchase_lines l
   LEFT JOIN r ON l.po=r.po
   AND l.line=r.line)
SELECT part
FROM a
GROUP BY part
HAVING MAX(received>=quantity)=0
exercises.reason: Express the universal rule by ruling out any complete or over-received line.

exercises.title: Status at inspection dates
exercises.prompt: For each dated inspection in inspection_visits return visit id and count of orders on that equipment whose latest event status by visit day was Open. Highest event ID breaks date ties.
exercises.sql:
SELECT v.id,
  (SELECT COUNT(*)
   FROM work_orders w
   WHERE w.equipment_code=v.equipment
     AND
       (SELECT status
        FROM order_events e
        WHERE e.wo=w.id
          AND e.event_date<=v.visit_date
        ORDER BY event_date DESC,
                 id DESC
        LIMIT 1)='Open')
FROM inspection_visits v
exercises.reason: Correlate on both the asset and the visit cutoff; current order status can differ from historical status.

exercises.title: Reconcile three reporting grains
exercises.prompt: For each equipment location return location, distinct asset count, open order count and booked labor value on open orders. Include locations with no open work. Return zero for missing measures.
exercises.sql:
WITH l AS
  (SELECT wo,
          SUM(hours*rate) v
   FROM labor_entries
   GROUP BY wo),
     a AS
  (SELECT w.equipment_code,
          COUNT(*) n,
          SUM(COALESCE(l.v, 0)) v
   FROM work_orders w
   LEFT JOIN l ON l.wo=w.id
   WHERE w.status='Open'
   GROUP BY w.equipment_code)
SELECT e.location,
       COUNT(*),
       SUM(COALESCE(a.n, 0)),
       SUM(COALESCE(a.v, 0))
FROM equipment e
LEFT JOIN a ON a.equipment_code=e.code
GROUP BY e.location
exercises.reason: Reduce labor to orders, then orders to assets. The final location group can safely add the measures without multiplying assets.

exercises.title: Asset locations
exercises.prompt: List location and asset code ordered by location then code.
exercises.sql: SELECT location, code FROM equipment ORDER BY location, code
exercises.reason: Use both requested sort keys.

exercises.title: PM interval register
exercises.prompt: Show basis, interval and schedule code ordered by code.
exercises.sql: SELECT basis, interval_value, code FROM pm_schedules ORDER BY code
exercises.reason: Read intervals together with their units.

exercises.title: Stock buffers
exercises.prompt: Show store, part and quantity above reorder level, sorted by store and part.
exercises.sql: SELECT store, part, quantity-reorder_level FROM stock ORDER BY store, part
exercises.reason: Subtract the threshold even when the result is negative.

exercises.title: Order cost range
exercises.prompt: Show status, lowest cost and highest cost by status, sorted by status.
exercises.sql: SELECT status, MIN(cost), MAX(cost) FROM work_orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY status
exercises.reason: Group by the workflow status.

exercises.title: Meter coverage
exercises.prompt: Show each meter code and number of readings, including empty meters, ordered by code.
exercises.sql: SELECT m.code, COUNT(r.id) FROM meters m LEFT JOIN meter_readings r ON r.meter=m.code GROUP BY m.code ORDER BY m.code
exercises.reason: Count the nullable reading identifier.

exercises.title: PM coverage by asset
exercises.prompt: Show asset code and number of associated schedules for every asset ordered by code.
exercises.sql: SELECT e.code, COUNT(p.code) FROM equipment e LEFT JOIN pm_schedules p ON p.equipment=e.code GROUP BY e.code ORDER BY e.code
exercises.reason: Preserve equipment with no schedule.

exercises.title: Latest meter sample
exercises.prompt: Return meter, date and reading for the most recent sample per meter. Break date ties by greatest ID and sort by meter.
exercises.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY meter ORDER BY reading_date DESC,id DESC) AS n FROM meter_readings) SELECT meter,reading_date,reading FROM ranked WHERE n=1 ORDER BY meter
exercises.reason: Rank readings inside each meter.

exercises.title: Failure-code tally
exercises.prompt: A shift log contains LEAK, SEIZE and LEAK. Use a VALUES CTE to return failure code and incident count ordered by count descending then code. This log is supplied in the prompt.
exercises.sql: WITH log(code) AS (VALUES ('LEAK'),('SEIZE'),('LEAK')) SELECT code,COUNT(*) FROM log GROUP BY code ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC,code
exercises.reason: Group the three supplied incidents by code.

exercises.title: Unissued reservations
exercises.prompt: Return distinct work order, part and store for reservations with no matching material issue on all three keys. Sort by those keys.
exercises.sql: SELECT DISTINCT r.wo,r.part,r.store FROM reservations r WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM material_issues i WHERE i.wo=r.wo AND i.part=r.part AND i.store=r.store) ORDER BY r.wo,r.part,r.store
exercises.reason: Test absence using the full reservation context.

exercises.title: Cumulative asset cost
exercises.prompt: For each order return asset, order ID and cumulative cost for that asset through that ID. Sort by asset then ID.
exercises.sql: SELECT equipment_code,id,SUM(cost) OVER(PARTITION BY equipment_code ORDER BY id ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) FROM work_orders ORDER BY equipment_code,id
exercises.reason: Partition by asset and order the window by order ID.
